proposals.evidence: The primary Hindi vegetable table, visually checked at PDF page 11 item 4, gives फूलगोबी “cauliflower”. Platts p. 858 independently lists phūl-kobī. The survey forms preserve the entire flower-plus-cabbage compound, with pʰ/f/ɸ and g/k or b/p regional adaptations; their precise Indo-Aryan transmission remains provisional. Existing Hindi pʰūlgobī “cauliflower” is the provisional donor, under the user’s preference to link supported cross-IA families. An intermediate Indo-Aryan language or another lending locality remains possible; the attestation locality is not claimed as the historical lending site.

proposals.evidence: The existing Rohili Hindi ṭamaṭar tomato attestation is independently supported by the visually checked primary Hindi table, PDF page 11 item 3 टमाटर. The selected r-ending survey forms preserve this whole regional loan word, with vowel and dental/retroflex transcription differences retained. Forms resembling a separate direct tomato adaptation without final r are not included. Existing Hindi ṭamaṭar “tomato” is the provisional donor, under the user’s preference to link supported cross-IA families. An intermediate Indo-Aryan language or another lending locality remains possible; the attestation locality is not claimed as the historical lending site.
